en.strong_distractor: b — Option (b) swaps the Treaty of Salbai's outcome description with that of the Convention of Wadgaon, which appeals to students who remember 'Salbai = British retained something' without specifics.
elimination_logic: Confirm A-3: Treaty of Surat (1775) — Raghoba ceded Salsette and Broach to British; this is a locked anchor pair.
Confirm D-4: Convention of Wadgaon (1779) — rare British military reversal requiring British withdrawal; anchor this.

Distinguish B and C: Salbai (1782) ended the First Anglo-Maratha War with British retaining Salsette and 20-year peace (B-1); Warren Hastings repudiated Wadgaon but this belongs to the Salbai context — his coordinated multi-front response (C-2) describes his strategic reaction to Wadgaon.
Only option (d) A-3, B-1, C-2, D-4 is consistent with all confirmed pairings.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The entity-swap trap targets the Warren Hastings connection. Students know Hastings was central to both repudiating Wadgaon and securing Salbai; they may assign his 'repudiation action' to Salbai rather than correctly placing it as his response to Wadgaon. Option (b) exploits this by shuffling B and C while keeping A and D fixed — forcing students to distinguish Hastings's reaction (to Wadgaon) from the treaty outcome (Salbai).
en.final_explanation:
The First Anglo-Maratha War (1775–1782) involved multiple agreements that must be carefully distinguished.

Correct pairings:
• A (Treaty of Surat, 1775) — 3 (Raghoba cedes Salsette and Broach to British in exchange for military support): The initiating event that drew British into Maratha succession dispute.
• B (Treaty of Salbai, 1782) — 1 (British retain Salsette, 20-year peace agreed, war ends): The war-ending agreement; British kept Salsette despite the broadly status quo nature of other provisions.
• C (Warren Hastings's strategic response) — 2 (Repudiation of Wadgaon Convention, coordinated multi-front military pressure from Bengal and Madras): Hastings rejected the Bombay army's Wadgaon surrender and reorganised the entire campaign strategy.
• D (Convention of Wadgaon, 1779) — 4 (Humiliating British withdrawal; rare Maratha military success over the Bombay army): The tactical Maratha victory that Hastings then worked to reverse.

Value Addition:
• Wadgaon (1779) is the only significant British battlefield defeat by Maratha forces — frequently tested.
• Salbai's 20-year peace clause delayed the Second Anglo-Maratha War to 1803.
• The First Anglo-Maratha War demonstrated that neither side could deliver a knockout blow — setting up the structural pattern of subsequent Anglo-Maratha conflicts.

shared.concept_anchor: Maneuver warfare — Palkhed strategy applied to principle

en.display_text:
An 18th-century Indian commander, rather than seeking a direct pitched battle with a stronger enemy force, positions his more mobile cavalry force behind the adversary's lines, systematically cutting off supply routes, intercepting reinforcement columns, and denying the enemy access to food and ammunition. Within weeks, the enemy force, despite superior numbers, is compelled to surrender and negotiate on the commander's terms — without a major engagement having taken place.

This military strategy most directly exemplifies which of the following tactical or strategic concepts?

(a) Scorched-earth warfare — deliberate destruction of resources to deny the enemy operational sustenance
(b) Positional defence strategy — holding strongly fortified positions to exhaust an advancing enemy force
(c) Maneuver warfare through enemy supply line interdiction — achieving objectives by making the adversary's position logistically untenable
(d) The political doctrine of Hindu Pad Padshahi — using military campaigns as instruments of establishing ideological Maratha paramountcy
en.strong_distractor: d — Option (d) is a strong distractor because the scenario describes a brilliant indirect approach, and students who know Baji Rao I's 'Hindu Pad Padshahi' ideology may associate any Baji Rao I strategy with that concept rather than the specific tactical principle.
elimination_logic: Eliminate option (a) — scorched-earth warfare involves destroying resources in one's own or enemy territory; the scenario describes interdicting supply lines without scorching, and the commander is not destroying local resources.
Eliminate option (b) — positional defence involves holding strong defensive positions; the scenario describes offensive mobility, not defensive positioning.
Eliminate option (d) — 'Hindu Pad Padshahi' is an ideological/political concept, not a tactical doctrine; the scenario describes a tactical method, not an imperial ideology.

Confirm option (c) — interdiction of enemy supply lines to force capitulation without pitched battle is precisely the maneuver warfare tactic used at Palkhed (1728); the scenario maps exactly to this principle.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: Option (d) targets students who associate any description of Baji Rao I's military brilliance with 'Hindu Pad Padshahi'. That concept is a political ideology (Maratha paramountcy), not a tactical doctrine. The scenario describes a specific tactical method — maneuver warfare through supply interdiction — which is the principle exemplified at Palkhed, not an expression of political philosophy. Students who recall 'Baji Rao I = Hindu Pad Padshahi' without distinguishing ideology from tactics will select (d).
en.final_explanation:
This scenario reconstructs the strategic logic of the Battle of Palkhed (1728) without naming it — testing principle recognition rather than event recall.

Applicable principle: Maneuver warfare through enemy supply line interdiction — achieving military objectives by forcing the adversary into an untenable logistical position rather than engaging in a direct pitched battle.

यह सैन्य रणनीति निम्नलिखित सामरिक या रणनीतिक अवधारणाओं में से किसका सबसे प्रत्यक्ष उदाहरण है?

(a) जला-भुना युद्ध — शत्रु को परिचालन पोषण से वंचित करने के लिए संसाधनों का जानबूझकर विनाश

यह परिदृश्य पालखेड की लड़ाई (1728) की रणनीतिक तर्क को बिना नाम लिए पुनर्निर्मित करता है — घटना की पुनरावृत्ति के बजाय सिद्धांत की पहचान का परीक्षण करता है।

लागू सिद्धांत: शत्रु की आपूर्ति लाइनों को बाधित करके युद्धकला — प्रत्यक्ष युद्ध में शामिल हुए बिना विरोधी को असहनीय रसद स्थिति में डालकर सैन्य उद्देश्य प्राप्त करना।

परिदृश्य से मेल: सेनापति सीधे मुकाबले से बचता है, शत्रु की पंक्तियों के पीछे जाता है, आपूर्ति और सहायता को काटता है, और थकावट के माध्यम से समर्पण को मजबूर करता है — ठीक वैसा ही जैसा बाजी राव प्रथम ने निज़ाम-उल-मुल्क के विरुद्ध पालखेड में किया।

• विकल्प (a) — जला-भुना युद्ध: गलत। जला-भुना युद्ध में संसाधनों (खेत, आपूर्ति डिपो, शहर) को जानबूझकर नष्ट करना शामिल है ताकि शत्रु को उनसे वंचित किया जा सके। परिदृश्य आपूर्ति मार्गों को बाधित करने का वर्णन करता है, क्षेत्र को नष्ट करने का नहीं।
• विकल्प (b) — स्थिति रक्षा रणनीति: गलत। परिदृश्य एक आक्रामक युद्धकला का वर्णन करता है; स्थिति रक्षा एक निष्क्रिय, क्षेत्र बनाए रखने वाली रणनीति है।
• विकल्प (c) — आपूर्ति लाइन बाधा के माध्यम से युद्धकला: सही। सेनापति की घेराबंदी, आपूर्ति काटने, और पूर्ण युद्ध के बिना समर्पण को मजबूर करने की रणनीति इस सामरिक दृष्टिकोण की विशेषता है — और पालखेड की भी।
• विकल्प (d) — सैन्य अभियानों में हिंदू पद पदशाही विचारधारा का प्रयोग: गलत। यह मराठा सर्वोच्चता को व्यक्त करने वाली राजनीतिक विचारधारा है — सामरिक सिद्धांत नहीं।

मूल्यवर्धन:
• पालखेड (1728) को सैन्य अकादमियों में अप्रत्यक्ष दृष्टिकोण युद्धकला के प्रारंभिक उदाहरण के रूप में पढ़ाया जाता है।
• अप्रत्यक्ष दृष्टिकोण — रसद के माध्यम से विजय प्राप्त करना, सीधे मुकाबले के बजाय — आक्रमणकारियों के लिए हताहतों को कम करता है।
• पालखेड के बाद मुँगी-शेगांव संधि इस सामरिक कौशल का राजनीतिक परिणाम थी।
